artifact_method: Sealed independent strict DER parser plus direct RSA modular exponentiation using public res/keys; no signer import or private key read

negative_tests.name: P291 key instead of RK key

private_identity_binding.method: Independent ELF32 symbol/object/Go string pointer+length within PT_LOAD

static_checks: Exact RK3229-C recovery map and private eMMC identity are required before selection and revalidated during capture. Other units and Android partition numbering are not substituted.
All eligible ordinary partitions are ordered by physical start; backup p10 is last. Whole eMMC user-area capture is prohibited so it cannot include backup indirectly.
Existing mounted-RW/superblock/holders/swap guards remain. Cache RW remains omitted; nothing is remounted or changed to force eligibility.
Only exact p10/179:10/64MiB/backup aliases may use the new branch. It requires a memory callback and remains last in the plan.

Memory guard requires 64MiB data plus 64MiB margin. MemAvailable is preferred; Linux 3.10 fallback requires MemTotal >=512MiB, valid kB fields and checked arithmetic, subtracting Shmem, Dirty and Writeback.
Backup is read completely into RAM, source is closed/revalidated/reopened and reread for SHA. No backup destination part is created unless both source hashes match.
After equality, RAM bytes are written to one exclusive SD file, synced, closed and reread. Copy SHA and SD SHA must equal both source reads; final identity and directory sync remain required.
Any mismatch or IO/revalidation/sync failure remains fatal. Previous verified sources remain in failed-report.json; a failed source is not accepted as stable.
Ordinary captureOne and following helper bodies are unchanged from 0.2. capture_test, Linux block/SD adapter and SD policy bytes are unchanged.
Internal blocks remain O_RDONLY. No O_DIRECT, mount, unmount, remount, format, flash, raw write, reboot, network operation or USB fallback is introduced.
Recorded source_policy and optional verification_order are validated by the full PC reader. Whole disk and wrong backup ordering are rejected.

Partial PC reader retains authoritative failure markers and counts only sources with verified part states plus matching copy/source-reread/PC hashes. Failed backup bytes cannot become a completed capture.

SD preparer pins the acquisition receipt and validates the exact nine previous files before changes. It identifies SD and Kingston, verifies archived predecessors, stages/re-reads two new files, then replaces only the two old known files and rechecks seven preserved files.

tests_scope.go_host_environment: Windows amd64; events include subtests and groups
tests_scope.new_buffered_tests: Ordering; memory and both source failures before any backup file; destination/sync/revalidation errors; full 64MiB simulated mismatch preserves preceding verified source
tests_scope.reader_skip: OS does not permit this test account to create symbolic links

nonblocking_observations: The first RK3 build was rejected before signing because trimpath omits ldflags from Go build-info. It was preserved. Final build retains ELF symbols and verifies the actual Go string, rather than the presence of a command in metadata.
Four-entry ZIP still has no META-INF/com/android/metadata. RK2 entered the extractor despite that warning; final RK3 acceptance remains pending.
No universal deadline can interrupt blocked kernel IO. Memory accounting is an estimate, so allocation or a host crash can still interrupt receipt creation.
limitations: This is code, PC artifact and recorded-inventory validation, not a physical execution of RK3.
Both source reads use normal buffered kernel IO. Their agreement does not demonstrate uncached physical reads, a stopped writer or an atomic snapshot.
Observed p10 mismatch does not establish the writer, SD failure, eMMC failure or malware. The RAM sequence is a changed experiment, not a confirmed repair to a known cause.
Recovery can write its own logs/cache/metadata although the extractor reads internal blocks only.
Busy/inaccessible regions remain omitted. No complete-device backup, firmware authenticity, malware absence, restoration or production trust is certified.
The publicly known Rockchip development trust is for laboratory compatibility, not exclusive remote-update security.
No volume flush, physical ejection, SD delivery or TV execution is certified by this independent review.
